text: If you love Civilization style games then you'll appreciate Endless Legend; even more so if you have a fondness for totally unique fantasy settings and a totally unseen take on the 4X genre. The inclusion of narratives, quests, seasons, meaningful minor factions, and long-term planning goals have pretty much made this game incredible despite being Early Access. Hell, I love this game so much that I'm writing a review for it.

It is an awesome game, I brought it when it was released back in 2005.
Based on the novel of same name by Dale Brown. Act of war Direct Action is an engaging game. It tells a thrilling story of power, politics and terror of possible near future due to energy crisis.
like typical strategy game it has 3 factions; they are well balanced and have their respective preferred tactics on the field.
US Army: you can generally expect the units to be the best in its class but lacks diversity, take example of the M1 tank, which has highest HP and firepower. It is very straight forward, easy to manage, learn and use.
Task force Talon: simply put: Jack of all trade but master of none, many of its units can fill in multiple roles, for example the Spinner Drones, can switch between anti-tank and anti-air, as well as bomb drone. also rely heavly on infantry, It has best infantry in the early on.
Consortium: is a stealthy, high tech faction rely heavly on stealth and ambush tactics.
All 3 factions have its version of superweapons or in this game, called Tactical weapon. Each faction has its way to counter it.
It has innovative resource system where encourage you to capture enemy troops while protect your own from being captured. especially in later stage of game.
And remember the Live action cutscenes videos from Westwood Studio? Yup, this game has it.
It is, after all, a 2005 game, so don't expect to have top notch game engine of modern strategy game, but it is still impressive. This game has odd resolution options at today's standard and lacks wide screen support; however it shouldn't matter once you get used to it.
It suffered from technical issues regarding the memory addressing, but I believe it is fixed with latest patch as I was able to fire it up on my laptop which has i7 processor, 12GB of ram, nvidia GT735 graphic processor and runs windows 8.1.

Both Act of War Games, have been finally updated to work on Modern Systems.
I have i7 CPU and Geforce 970 using windows 7, both games work and play good.
One minor complaint is Direct Action needs a community patch to run 1080p, but there is NO UI stretching and looks perfect when patch and AA forced from Nvidia Control Panel.
I'm not really much of online multiplayer gamer, so I have no idea if MP is alive or works at all. But the game does have AI Skirmish with a nice selection of maps.
Act of War is true classic, and I was always disappointed it never worked on modern machines. I am now delighted that it can be played once again. This game had stellar presentation for back in 2005. You should enjoy yourself if you like the idea of pseudo present day military RTS with Full Motion Video cutscenes with decent acting and good production values.

Act of war direct action is one of the brilliant strategy game ever made for me.Probably I must have played this more than 100 hours at non-steam version when it was first released.It's scenario was inspired from Dale Brown's stories (Who is well known military novel author like Tom Clancy).If you like Tom clancy style scenarios or series like 24,homeland etc you will probably like this game.
AoW:DA also looks similar C&C titles,building base,gathering petrol resources and producing units to crush enemy.Cutscenes is one of the best part of AoW.Which made with real actors.On missions a little video screen appears on the corner and begins to inform you about mission and shows news just like C&C.You can capture wounded enemy soldiers as a prisoner and sell it.
Game changing shape according to missions.Sometimes you control small tactical units to eliminate enemy forces or sometimes building bases and producing mass armies.
As far as I read around, some guys complain about that game doesn't work on windows 7 64 bit and more than 2 GB ram.I run windows 7 64 bit home premium and have 8 GB ram,I haven't experienced any problem with game.I just installed and hit the play button it launched.
Edit:A patch has been released for game to run on win7 and 8.1
+Good scenario

+C&C style videos
+Music

+never bored (it depends on you of course :) )

I wish a "neutral or not decided" review  would be possible, as far as I'm concerned, this game would fit right there.
Objectively, this game is relatively nice and well done (that's why I ended up pressing "Yes" instead or "No"). It's a tough game, but not really for the good reasons, or at least not the reasons I was expecting. It's not really a reflex game, it's more a memory game : if you play purely on reflexes, you'll fail more or less quickly. Instead, you have to "grind" levels, repeating them ad nauseam, until you recognize the incoming patterns, and know before reaching them what you're about to do. Worse, you need to remember those patterns at least twice (normal, and upside down, so to speak).
And since you start back at level 1 each time you die (i.e. every few seconds usually :D), getting and knowing level 3 for example, is already a real pita, as you don't reach it every time, far from it. Case in point : I made it to level 4, but never got past it, and at this point, I'm already bored (ok, I might be a bit too old for this kind of games, but still :p).
Besides, there are a few problems that make the matter worse :
- jumping (switching floor and ceiling) does not feel "natural" : it seems you're landing further than you would expect, leading to frustrating deaths or missing bonuses to collect.
- collisions also seem a bit off, espcecially (again) when jumping : you'll die often this way while thinking your jump was perfectly valid. I also saw a few cases where I went right though obstables.
The 2 above points could really be a problem for such a game, but you get used to them, eventually. UPDATED REVIEW 01/05/16
OVER 170 HOURS GAME PLAY
After the BETA update I decided to also update my review for the game there are some changes.
Tree of Life interesting survival game which has great potential but whether or not the developers communicate or not is a different matter. Currently in beta so it has many bugs and various issues but also some MAJOR issues which I will get in to.
In Tree of Life's current state there is much to improve on but there is still a lot of content there for everyone to enjoy so if you do wish to play Tree of Life in its beta state then please remember it is not the full game but you will have a good time depending on your neighbours.
Game play:
Tree of Life contains 25 skills that you can progress in which you can max only 8 so if you wish to become a fighter or builder then you can do so and ignore the skills you do not wish to progress in. However, there are some skills which you may not wish to progress in but you will be forced to level in e.g. If you want to create a weapon but that weapon requires an item that only a Tinkerer can create.
PvE:
There is a small amount of PvE but I think they are starting to focus on more of this. The basics are there but it is VERY basic. They have some "plans" in the making apparently, such as dungeons. But this has not been revealed exactly so who knows what they will be adding.
PvP:
There is much PvP which can be good or bad. PvP is extremely unbalanced as you can grief players by building all around their base and nothing can be done about it. The game punishes you If you try to prevent a griefer by turning you hostile rather than the griefer.
Grind:
This game is one of the biggest grinds I have seen in any game! The map is 4x bigger but you may have to travel for about 30mins to reach a special type of tree but as you reach your destination, there are none around as it has been farmed. You will be running back and forth for hours on end.
Wood Cutting Simulator:
Because there is a huge grind and that most items need wood, you will be cutting trees all day everyday! It is painfully slow and boring to cut wood and sometimes you may not even get any wood from a tree. I dint mind a small grind but the woodcutting is ridiculous!
In-Game Shop:
There is a shop where you can spend real money of items. This is fine and so far they are just bags with more slots and a mount. The only problem is the price. The prices for these items are extremely expensive. A mount costs £15.41 and the game costs £14.99!! Not only that but that mount is apparently 10% off!
Some Concerns:
I have around 100 hours into this game so far, made lots of friends (and enemies) and found a very friendly and active guild where we have spent a very long time improving our base and skills. I am having lots of fun but do get very frustrated with what has been updated in the game.
Now we have had a map wipe on 18/04/16 which is perfectly fine as it let us start from scratch, we were told the map would be 4x bigger (woohoo!), better graphics and more items etc have been added. Fantastic right? Wrong! 4x bigger is correct but they have hidden over half of the map! Covered it with thick fog not allowing us to see a thing and not allowing us to build in these areas! We were not told this before the map wipe so we had to suffer in silence.
Communication seems to be the biggest concern for me. There is some on the forum but if you dont sign up there then you will not be able to get as many updates. I know this is the beta but i feel like we have all been taken for a ride than we never wanted.
Pros:
Great graphics (it's not everyones cup of tea).
Many skills to choose from and level.
Huge map.
PVP/PVE (You don't have to PVP but prepare for it).
Criminal System (Not developed very well).
Bounty System (Not developed very well).
Friendly developers (When they actually communicate).
Feels different from other survival/sandbox games.
Monster villages which will attack player bases.
Just the right amount of challenge.
Cons:
Punishment for friendly players
Thick fog not allowing players to see/build half of the map.
Communication is very poor.
Bugs (It is Beta!).
Very little player customisation.
If your base is close to a raiding guild then prepare to log in every day to a raided base.
No fast travel on such a large map.
Real money in game shop is very expensive! For a bag it costs nearly as much as the actual game!
VERDICT:
DO NOT BUY IN CURRENT STATE!
In the games current state I would say wait a few more months. I hope they listen to our concerns because this game is not even in a beta stage in my opinion. They labeled it beta to get a flood of new customers and the game needs a hell of a lot more added to it. The only thing that keeps me playing Tree of Life is my guild members. We have put so much time into it that we do not want to put it to waste.

This shaping up to the be the 4X game of the year.
It's by the same guys who did Endless Space; their experience with the genre really shines through and it's sort of set in the same universe with similar mechanics. There are some areas they struggled with in the previous game; namely diplomacy and procedurally generated areas. The combat is vastly improved over the original Endless Space, and while there are glaring issues still with balance (AIs getting whupped by minor factions) it's all fairly simple to resolve.
There's also a superb choice of playstyles, including factions which cannot go to war but have access to anonymous mercaneries, a faction which cannot be "at peace" with anyone, some which are literalyl powered by magical dust and so forth.
Worth every penny if version 1 is half the game v0.581 is so far.

Endless Space was a work of art. But with limited competition in terms of modern space-based 4x games, it had the luxury of an easier benchmark to surpass. Endless Legend is Amplitudes leap into the world of land-based 4x, of which competition is more plentiful; and yet despite having bigger opponants to defeat, such as the dominating Civilization series, Endless Legend is showing signs that it just might set itself in stone as a game to be remembered.
Despite still having a few rough edges (mostly typos or grammar errors in text), Endless Legend shows promise; and that promise is the promise to dazzle us with beautiful artwork, breath-taking fantasy themes and action-packed gameplay. Stunning visuals, magnificent music and diverse factions truly make Auriga a world you want to get to know. A world you want to explore. A world you want to conquer. Be it as woodland-dwelling builders, powerful animated suits of armour, mysterious spellcasters or corpse-eating insectoids.
So think of it as Civilization mixed in with Endless Space with improved visuals, a fantasy settings and tactical combat. In fact, don't, because that doesn't do it justice. The only way to truly understand the charm and beauty of this game is to play it.
I recommend.

Highly recommended to all fans of Civilisation, Endless saga lovers and any gamer who enjoys a strategic game.

Technology trees and races are very refined with the entire game looking very polished. The new updated combat system may be a bit glass-cannon oreintated but I still find it original and interesting with many decisions to make each turn which makes this game pace feel much nicer.

Eventually, you’ll have a selection of 15 heroes to choose from (19 if you also purchased “Starstorm”) each with 2 special skills and a regular attack. Further levelling up of your profile will unlock special features for your skills, like lower cooldowns or larger range. So people who have played longer will have a wider variety of features in their skills.
Awesomenauts also doesn’t have a steep learning curve like other MOBA games, so it’s fairly easy to jump into the game and get playing. However, it’s still varied enough to not grow stale quickly and the skill ceiling is high enough to keep you playing and trying to improve.

Though pretty imbalanced with the introduction of new, paid-DLC characters who tend to throw things out of whack in the right hands, this game is everything that League of Legends strives for, without the long time investment per match and steep learning curve.
Side-scrolling MOBA with a touch of... Super Smash Brothers? No, but fighting games where one's performance in a fight is not based solely on their purchased gear in that particular match. The penalties for falling behind in level are not always as severe as those in stricter MOBAs such as DotA or LoL, but are still noticeable enough to keep you on the edge of your seat for the majority of the matches that aren't total landslide victories.
No pay to win. Excellent tuning for the original cast (and soon to be the DLC cast, if they can get around to patching things). Variety of maps and builds provide hours of entertainment without the action ever really getting stale. The leveling system, with multiple prestige tiers, while superficial, provides me with an artificial sense of progress that LoL sorely lacks at end-game, outside of the competitive spectrum.

Why haven't I been playing this game for years already? Clearly I'm some sort of idiot. This is all the FPS fix I ever wanted and needed. Yeah, the game is basically a gigantic Grind Quest to get stuff you possibly don't need but just kinda want, and it works because the gameplay is such fun. It's a sad state of affairs in the game industry that I even have to point that out, but there are so many gear and loot oriented games that forget the core gameplay is supposed to be great fun so the grind.....doesn't grind!
In Warframe the grind is an overarching objective, it's something you aim for in the long term. I want THAT thing. But I don't log in to grind, I'm logging in to PLAY. I'm logging in because even if I technically make zero progress in my long term grind-goal, I still want to spend an hour or two being a rampaging murder machine.
Graphically the game is solid despite its age, but it's not about fidelity, it's about aesthetic. Warframe is drowning in character. This is not a run of the mill sci-fi setting, with run of the mill designs. Honestly, I don't even LIKE a lot of the designs, but it's all so characterful and pulled off with such colour and creativity that it never puts me off despite so many things being subjectively ugly to me, because despite my personal preferences, this game stays consistent and.....dare I say it....immersive. Even if stuff is ugly it's still INTERESTING, I want to see more of it because it's just cool to see. I arrived outside a giant tower where some guys opened a rock and cut out a giant slab of meat that was in it, which landed with a heavy splat on the beach like a giant meat-mattress. I still don't know what that was all about, but MAN do I want to know more about the rockmeat village than I ever did about the billions of other nondescript villages I've visited in my gaming life.
At this point there's a huge array of Warframes (the battlesuit you control and which is effectively a 'class' in itself) to suit pretty much any style of play or aesthetic preference. Grind being the name of the game means it can take a real long time to get another, but here the game triumphs again by trying to keep the frames balanced. What this means is that you're not 'gimped' from using one of the starter frames; new frames mean new styles of play instead of just being directly better, so if all you ever wanted in life was to be an angry Unicorn O' Death, well then you feel completely free to use nothing but that starting Excalibur Warframe from now until forever.
Pretty much all the stuff in the game can be bought for real money. As already said with Warframes, they're meant to be balanced with each other so it really doesn't matter if you bought an 'endgame' Warframe at the beginning of your time with the game.....in fact at the lowest levels they'll largely all be about the basic run and gun gameplay anyway until you level up and get them fitted out with mods. I actually did this myself, there was a sale on Platinum, so I bought some, and hadn't even reached the third mastery level before I bought Mesa simply because it's the one I fell in love with when looking through the Warframe list! Weapons can also be bought, but only if you're a high enough level to use them, so no buying mega weapons before your time with real money.
So try it! It's free! You can play as much as you want before you choose to lay down some money to buy cool bits and pieces you want, or just never pay anything at all, or treat it as another resource to grind and sell things you find in-game for Platinum on the market. Whatever. I spent money almost immediately because I was having such fun, and knew being able to go around as Mesa looooooong before I could ever get her normally was going to be even more fun. But it's up to you.
My only word of warning to leave off with is to beware of the learning curve. Pretty much every game, no matter how good, does at least one thing wrong, and with Warframe it's obvious - the tutorials suck and there are some mission types and mechanics in the game that leave you running for a google search shouting, "BUT WHAT DO I ACTUALLY DOOOOOO!?" Bash through that though, it doesn't take long, and you can be happily slide-jumping about the place cutting Grineer in half and shooting the silly helmets off Corpus losers.
Oh, also, yes, the game is always online, but you can do everything solo if you want to. And yes, you CAN do it solo. It's not 'yeah you can technically go in alone but you'll get your s*** pushed in guaranteed', it's actually soloable and fun. Teaming just means more faces to shoot, bigger rewards, and people will actually see it when you do something ridiculously badass by accident.

So I am going to be a bit different and NOT complain about the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ DRM♥♥♥♥♥♥and talk about the actual game. Now I did play most of this game on my Xbox and Switch because of the two week delay for PC but the game is basaiclly the same aside from some audio issues on my Xbox version.
Now the design of the game is easily the second best part of it. The pixel graphics looks amazing. It keeps the old style look while modernizing it with more colors and animation frames. The classic stages are familiar yet so different when you play them especially during the second Act if the zone. They definitely encourage you to explore since their are two giant rings that will take you to the special stages to collect the Chaos Emeralds. Boss battles are fun and entertaining while still being a little difficult.
The gameplay is what the older Sonic fans like myself remembers. Although more refunded it handles the same, Sonic and friends are still terrifying to control on short surfaces and you will often fine yourself going to faster than you’d like and end up hitting an enemy. The added drop dash is very very fun to use, great for racing your friends and time trails. The special stages to collect the Chaos emeralds are easy and difficult at the same time. Once you figure out how to run them it’s easy but if you happen to get Mach 3 Speed you will occasionally lose control of the character and either jump to soon and hit a obstacle, or fall off the map. I prefer to hit Mach 2 and cruise my way to the emerald. Blue sphere stages are annoying as ever but not as difficult as it was in Sonic 3. The main issues I have with this game is that the abilities you unlock by collecting those emblems in the blue sphere zones is that you can only use those abilities in the games No Save file, which makes no sense since the abilities doesn’t make the main game easier.
Easily the best part of gameplay is getting the ability to use Super Sonic, Tails, and Knuckles. The power to run thought stages and obliterate bosses that gave you issues is super satisfying. However this is also dangerous as well in late game stages, as they are a little more confusing and can take longer to complete, that and being crushed out of Super is annoying enough. Sonic is the fastest of them all and is sometimes very challenging to platform with in the simplest of situations. Tails is a little slower if not just as fast as Sonic but can jump extremely high. Knuckles is easily the most disappointing super form. He feelings like a speed boost with invincibility. He’s not as fast as the other two and his jump height is pathetic, I use him the least. Lastly they recently added the ability to transform into Super forms with a different button rather than double tapping the jump button which removed the frustration of trying to use your current shield ability, fly, glide, or drop dash and transforming instead.
Lastly the music is easily the best part of the game. There is one stage I don’t like to much but other then that it’s beautiful. I enjoy the smooth transitions from act 1 to 2 with the music, the original stages are phenomenal and the classic stages are amazing. I am kinda sad that Flying Battery didn’t really change much but it’s still great.
This game is a much buy no matter if you are a old loyal fan like me or a new kid. This game is obviously beating on the door of nostalgia, but who cares it’s a really great game and I hope they make a sequel since they won’t be doing dlc :(.

Larian has done it again with another 10/10 clasic RPG experience. I cant wait for the EE for this beauty. Breakdown below.
Pros:
+++++Free complete respecs are available any time after act 1. Allows you a lot of room to experiment and discover what builds are the best/most fun.
+++Same great combat, build customization, and RPG experience from DOS1EE
++Lonewolf is back
++Race/preset lore choices on character creation
++Amazing mutliplayer support, up to 4 players
++PVP made more easy and fun though the declare war and online arena system
++Tons of flavor and unique items. Several kinds of items i have never seen in another RPG
+All the classes/builds are viable just like in DOS1
+New source point system tries to control spells that trivialize the game
+Great flavor and level design
+A classic soundtrack
+Open your game to the world and let people join or join random games
+Difficulty settings range from "wow are they even trying to hurt me" to "this fight will take multiple hours to figure out and clear"
+Many new races/enemy types
+Memory system prevents you from having to manage 3 full spell bars and makes characters feel more unique/specialized compared to the party.
Mixed/preference:
+/-Game is significantly harder than DOS1EE
+/-Some of the more broken spells and abilities have been removed
+/-CC has been massively nerfed
+/-Crafting has also been nerfed, but all crafting can be done from level 1
+/-Stealing has been slightly nerfed, now after you steal you have to portal away for a few min to let the heat die down.
Cons:
-Source point controls are easily bypassed, but are also cumbersomely attached to abilities are are needed to do basic things out of combat, like bless. The game also disincentivises experimenting with new abilities if they have source point costs, because you have to refill the source points after. Some abilities are attached to source points that are clearly not good enough to warrant the source point cost, and the ability will never be used.
-some people report lots of bugs, but I have done many playthroughs and have not encountered anything that I could not resolve in-game
-cant dye your outfits anymore
-with the new system, tons of things have been removed. No more weapon or armor modification except poisoning and adding runes.
--No orcs (c'mon man wtf)
---Parties with split damage types (magic/physical) are heavily penalized by the new armor system. Biggest gripe by far. If your party is split 2-2 the game will be much harder. If you have 3 physical damage and 1 magic damage, the magic damage hero will often feel like it isnt contributing much to the encounters unless it is summon/support.
Overall the game is absolutely amazing. I may have a lot of cons on that list, but just like a spouse, its easy to nit-pick the flaws  of something you love so much. Additionally, I am comparing the release version of DOS2 to the EE version of DOS1. I strongly encourage anyone who likes RPGs or is interested in a more classic/hardcore RPG experience. You will not regret it.

As a big Civ V fan, I was desperately looking for an alternative after having spent over 600 hours conquering the known world. I'm always skeptical at fantasy clone of civ, because since Master of Magic back in the 90's no developer has ever managed to create a balanced 4x fantasy game. Even the recent Warlock series become way too easy in end game when powerful spells just break the game.
Endless Legend however, althought being set in a fantasy world, avoids the "magic trap" (you can't research or cast spells) by offering a profound and refreshing approach to the 4x genre. The game revolves more around resource management, city improvement and map exploration, rather than combat. Think of it of as a Game of Thrones Manager 2014, where you keep control over regions by either dominating the minor factions that inhabit them by force or diplomacy. Aslo the graphical environment reminds me a lot of the GoT opening credits style.
Right now the game is far from being finished now, and the two main reasons I haven't poured more hours into this game are the simplistic AI (no diplomacy, they keep just eventually declaring war to you and senselessy send some units attack you) and the lack of multiplayer.
I don't want to spoil moreof the surprises that await you in Endless Legends, but let me tell you this: If you're a true Civilization lover, you can't do anything wrong with this game.
One last tip: there's no tutorial and the interface can be quite intimidating. Go to YouTube and take an hour to get introduced to it, lots of nice videos there.

Don't turn a blind eye on this game, saying 'Just another 4XStrategy Game'. Well it is just another one, with its own little spin. I'm talking about gameplay mechanics which set this game apart from the likes of Civilization or other 4X games - A few of these features might actually come as a surprise and make this game worth its while. Think of it as Endless Space, well just that suddenly different nations, alien to one another, crashlanded on a planet which already harbored life, bound to be integrated into the empires, so that one may reign supreme.
Right from the start of the game you notice the differences, instead of singular troops you move whole armies, sometimes accompanied by Heroes with their own set of skills and items. Talking about items, you can create new troop layouts with better equipment throughout the game and change up the game with the resources you harvested, suddenly your basic archer squad that died to the roaming armies, now takes them on with ease.
Combat itself works a lot like it does in Endless Space, just that you position your troops on uneven terrain, target your enemies and roll for iniative! - Combat itself is simulated and several armies, which stand nearby can partake.
The roaming armies I spoke of are the native races of the planet, which can be integrated to gain a minor bonus for your empire and will follow you willingly into war against your enemies.
The main important feature that I wish to talk about however is the founding of cities. It is alike that of Civ yet very different at the same time: The land is split into regions filled with different encampments, resources and important structures. A region becomes yours as soon as a city is founded in it. So expand your territory wisely, otherwise you might not be able to gain supremecy over your enemies, be they bots or since a recent update human players, fulfill your quest to find out the truth (Yes there is an actual storyline for each nation) and immerse yourself in a beautifully crafted game, which keeps on getting better.
The devs certainly know where they are going with this.
Check it out, it really is more than worth the money,

I have enjoyed the game immensely because it brings together several aspects that I always desired from strategic games;
1. Centered around economy and constantly building up all of your cities (as opposed to simply trying to destroy your opponents, though you can also take over other people's things).
2. Despite being heavilly driven by economy, you can build armies and conquer other people through force as well.
3. Advantages of peace, with trading and sharing of technologies.
4. Choice in technologies (now all of them are fairly good, and eventually you can choose all, but sometimes you have to make a few sacrifices to get to the higher ones first :) )
5. Multiple Interesting Races (6 so far, 8 coming) each with different strategies.
6. A constantly changing environment (the game creates an entirely random setting each time you make a new game, which is lovely <3 ) and perfect for replaying and multi-player gaming with friends.
7. Ruins, minor factions, and ocean travel for the explorer in you.
8. Turns instead of all at once (now while I can see why the alternative some people would like, I think it takes away from the strategic of it and would make things too much 'who can click the fastest' type of game, luckilly this isn't that.. you can spend an hour if you want in a non-timed game turn, there isn't a constant rush.
9. Endless time, even though it does announce a winner at turn 200, you can keep on playing, keep getting different resources, keep building up massive cities, learning new technologies, and exploring the very far corners of the world if you haven't. (this is unlike wherein warcraft resources are limited, or in battles of middle earth where it all becomes the same).
10. Cities can be expanded to near limitless dimentions (atleast till they take up an entire region, which probably wouldn't happen unless you really tried)
This is my favorite strategic game of all time, and I look forward to whatever they do to expand it :) (( Come on Cultists and a water race.. we're waiting :3 )

This is a very simple game, where you kill goblins trying to reach the top of a tower by quickly pressing the key that matches its color. There are no levels or storyline, and just one life. That's it. You can unlock some characters and cosmetic changes to the tower, but they do not affect the game at all.
Its mechanics are quite reminiscent of ancient times (I dare say at a "Game&Watch" level). As far as I'm concerned, and as a counterpoint to other reviews, I'd say that's neither good or bad, it depends on your preferences. I personally enjoyed it, just like I enjoyed playing LCD games in the 80's, even though I realize that we are in 2015 and sensibilities have changed.
Unfortunaletly, all of this gets old quite fast, once you realize you have reached your reflex plateau. Some of us are old now. Since achievements are completely bugged, the incentives for longer play is removed. One I beat the 1000 point barrier, I did not see a reason to keep playing.
I'll say that I personally had a good time for the 3-4 hours I got out of it, and for that I'll vote "yes". But I would not recommed it unless it happens to be in a bundle (luckily, that's how I got it) or some kind of bargain. It's also true that I have played much better indie games for the same price.

Simply put, this is THE best game I have ever had the pleasure of experiencing, honestly it is that good.
Its not a game, its a masterpiece, an epic, an experience.
I am not sure how to put into words how good it is, but I can try.
I went into the game at first with a friend playing co-op, having not played the first divinity sin. While I have played my fair share of RPG's and turn based games alike, I wasnt sure what to expect. What I got blew me away. The story, the characters, the sheer scale and depth of the world and the game is mind-blowing. In a time when the games industry has turned into a machine, churning out half-baked repetitive, microtransaction full 'games'. It is refreshing to find a game that has so much heart and soul put into it. The fact it was kickstarted as well, is just amazing. (Honestly if theres another kickstarter, just take my money)
The story follows you (either a 'origins' character, or a custom one) on your way to Fort Joy, this area is a single Island, and essentially acts as the tutorial/prologue section, here you get used to the mechanics, and decide how you like to spec your characters. You will meet a variety of people who can travel with you, all with their own backstorys and agendas. this area actually features a few bosses and multiple routes to take, if you take your time with it, which you should, it can easily take up to 30 hours to just complete this section.
Now one of the great things is the fact that, after this, you can re-spec any of your charcaters (including companions) at any time, from mage to knight, from summoner to battlemage. This proves very helpful, and a feature you dont see very often in RPG's. (You of course will need the gold to buy the equipment and skills for your change though)
The game took me and a friend around 90/100 hours to complete, and we still missed sections. And it was the best 100 hours I have ever spent gaming in my life. I seriously got attached to every character in the party and it felt great to complete their personal quests, seriously, do Lohse's personal quest, you wont regret it, actually had me almost in tears.
So onto the not so good (it 's amazing, but every game has it's flaws) parts, the last act (Arx, though this is one of the shorter acts) has a rushed feel about it, some fights start introducing some gimmicks to make it harder, but end up just being annoying and unbalanced. (Looking at you, embassy) Some fights become ridiculusly easy, while others just steamroll you. It also easily the most bugged part of the game, (although I still havent run into anything game-breaking).
The ending (I will try not to spoil, honest) leaves a bitter sweet taste in the mouth, while overall it's fine, theres no correlation between your character and your actions up until that point, and your companions descions and personal development (Lohse), as well as your love interest. It feels disjointed, and feels like it just ignores the game, and just leaves it up to you. (Some might like that, personally I dont).
The combat while fluid and quite frankly, great. Does have the habit at times, of descending into a necrofire free for all. Which, isnt that bad, but just feels like it detracts from the normally quite tactical and enjoyable turn based combat.
Overall, it has some minor flaws in relation to the final act/ending. I know others have experienced a fair few bugs as well (although I have not experienced many) But remains a fantastic experience with deep characters, an amazing world and fluid combat.
Seriously Buy It.

There aren't much to write home about this game because in its current state (version 0.5 as non-early access, wow), its gameplay mechanics and content is fairly one-dimensional. Pressing the right buttons to take down the goblins could have been so much more than depending on the player's quick wit that involves synesthesia (association with colors) to progress well. Doing the same thing over again does get somewhat tiring and both the upgrades as well as unlockable characters aren't enough to break from the monotony that the game suffers from. I don't even get informed how much mana I've earned in one session to tell how much chance I have to earn a gem (a sort unlocking currency).
There are some aspects to this game that are positive, nonetheless. I did just mention that the upgrades and unlockables were minor contents that gave an underwhelming replay value but I must admit that they are the important foundation to that value, which is appreciated. While the music somewhat clashes with the rogue-like graphics of The Tower Of Elements, it does give a slight sense of epicness and a dash of melancholy to the grey, medieval environment of the game's tower level.
The reviewers have complained that the controls haven't been explained to them, which I think must have been updated later because I grasped the game quite quickly. The option to use other controls such as the gamepad (heck, even the touchscreen), is a welcome feature. I think it would have been nice if you were able to tweak the controls to cast the color spells as you see fit.
I understand if it's one of those first games the developer has brought out and is currently working to flesh it out yet at this bare state, I am baffled that it's up on Steam already. There is a huge void for improvement and additional features to add to the gameplay's consistency. That's all there is to it as I write this review, but it remains to see if the promised multiplayer mode will change things from here.

I have enjoyed the game immensely because it brings together several aspects that I always desired from strategic games;
1. Centered around economy and constantly building up all of your cities (as opposed to simply trying to destroy your opponents, though you can also take over other people's things).
2. Despite being heavilly driven by economy, you can build armies and conquer other people through force as well.
3. Advantages of peace, with trading and sharing of technologies.
4. Choice in technologies (now all of them are fairly good, and eventually you can choose all, but sometimes you have to make a few sacrifices to get to the higher ones first :) )
5. Multiple Interesting Races (6 so far, 8 coming) each with different strategies.
6. A constantly changing environment (the game creates an entirely random setting each time you make a new game, which is lovely <3 ) and perfect for replaying and multi-player gaming with friends.
7. Ruins, minor factions, and ocean travel for the explorer in you.
8. Turns instead of all at once (now while I can see why the alternative some people would like, I think it takes away from the strategic of it and would make things too much 'who can click the fastest' type of game, luckilly this isn't that.. you can spend an hour if you want in a non-timed game turn, there isn't a constant rush.
9. Endless time, even though it does announce a winner at turn 200, you can keep on playing, keep getting different resources, keep building up massive cities, learning new technologies, and exploring the very far corners of the world if you haven't. (this is unlike wherein warcraft resources are limited, or in battles of middle earth where it all becomes the same).
10. Cities can be expanded to near limitless dimentions (atleast till they take up an entire region, which probably wouldn't happen unless you really tried)
This is my favorite strategic game of all time, and I look forward to whatever they do to expand it :) (( Come on Cultists and a water race.. we're waiting :3 )

This game haunts my dreams...
Keep in mind that i have played 70+ hours off line (in office,hope i'll not lose my job) and only ONE faction because i simply cannot get them out of my mind...
Greatest pros.The world.Its an alien world,one you have not encounter in any other game (except for those who own endless space).The factions are unique,from my favorite lich knights,fighting between honor and,vital for their survival,soul consuming,to the adept mages or "pain"mages and tech loving vaulters,all factions are more or less unique.The world itself have some very strange "anomalies" aka resources and some even more strange neutral tribes,like barbarians in civs,with the exception that after you conquer them,or bride them,or even do some quests for them you can add them to your army!In short the game world resemble Alpha Centauri after playing Civ.Alien,strange,unique and disturbing beautiful.
The map resemble the game of thrones intro map,with more details.There are hills,mountains,rivers,forests,swamps that add tactical value in battle and city building-planing.As you can see from the screenshots the world map is like nothing you have ever met in any other game!
Tactical combat may seem somewhat "hollow",as you can only deploy your troops and then choose their targets or the tile to move on,but after some battles you'll realize that its not that simple as it seems.There are many parameters that count in battle such as height,wooded areas,swamps,capabilities a unit can have such as soul liching.And you can change the armour and the weapons of your units to make even stronger,more defensive or more aggressive etc.The downside effect from equiping your units with the latest and heaviest armour possible,its an initiative value decrease and more turns to build it.Combat take place on the map tiles you meet the enemy,so its imperative to choose the battlefield wisely,even more if the enemy outnumbers your army.
The values that count ingame are quite common,dust for coinage,materials for building/training,food and research.There are many luxury resources,that keep your population happy,and more important military resources that allow you to build stronger armours and deadliest weapons to outfit your units.
Diplomacy is still under costruction,but there are many options other from war and peace,such as alliances,trade pacts and many more.One faction which is trade oriented cannot declare war (although they have strong defencive armies and a trade embargo capability that can be really pain in the #%@#!?) and another faction is in a costant war mode (necrophages) because of their all consuming or die nature.
The market.You can hire heroes,units,trade resources that your areas lack or have in abundance (military resources to build that shining new armour),all these options are quite common.BUT you can hire privateers,mercenary units that bare no banners and attack your enemies without declaring war.An option quite unique,that is quite useful in certain circumstances.
The game is still in a beta face,there are many features still missing,but its quite stable (never had a crash),it can run on a low-middle spec machine really nice (mine is i5,8gb ram,int.graph.card) and the immersion is its greatest value.Great story,unique factions and neutrals and a world you have never met before.

I have a long and sordid history with this game.  It is the reason I bought an Xbox 360 over a decade ago.  Quests are great, the world is huge, there is a lot to do.  Bethesda moved away from the clunky combat of Morrowind.  However, it also has fatal flaws with its levelling system and level-scaling - to the point that I cannot recommend the vanilla game as an RPG.
I have since again abandoned consoles and become a PC-only gamer once again.  I purchased the game again on sale to add to my collection as the game does have plenty to offer and can be had for very cheap.  With mods, you can fix the problems and make the game worth your efforts.  Be warned, the aforementioned problems ruin the game as a RPG and the combat really isn't great enough to make it worthwhile as an action game.  However, if you can get past its short-comings (which totally ruined the experience for me once I became aware of how bad they were) or are willing to tinker around enough with modding, then you will find a lot of value here.

This and Age of Empires 2 were my two first and greatest loves.
IMHO the game still holds up to this day, although I might be under the influence of nostalgia. The graphics are still good-looking, and at times even quite beautiful. Both expansions are worthwhile, with Shivering Isles being the greater of the two.
There are a lot of interesting sidequests, dungeons, easter eggs. The guilds are fun, especially the Assassin one.
The downsides may be centered around the main story, as well as dungeon conception. A lot of dungeons just look alike, and the Oblivion Gates quickly become tiresome to deal with. As for the story, it's not bad, but it's not very memorable either. I never really got attached to the main character, in fact I found some of the guild plotlines more compelling. However this might all come down to personnal preference.
Still a great game to explore and enjoy, and I hope you do .

The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion is a game developed by Bethesda Game Studios and published by Bethesday Softworks and 2K Games. I've played all of the Elder Scrolls series from The Elder Scrolls: Arena to this The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion. This game has amazing open world gameplay with beautiful graphics and massive content. Honestly, after playing 25+ hours I'm still not finished with what Elder Scrolls IV has to offer!
However, with its age and when it came out, there has been occasional voice acting issues and some occasional glitches
Overall, the graphics are a little outdated but still beautiful. The world is every bit as expansive as you might expect from an Elder Scrolls game. The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion improves on so much of what was introduced in The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind, and when played, it's easy to see what was kept and refined for The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
The game is fun. With a world this massive, and mechanics this complex, there are bound to be a few bugs. And there are. But they are remarkably far and few between for such a huge game, and the polish really shows
The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion is a fantastic edition to the Elder Scrolls series!

While I can say it's overall a really neat concept with a 2d MOBA, this game has a bit more focus on slightly more casual play. Along with quite a bit of humour thrown in there.  This would seem like a quite ideal time sink if you want to play between 15+ minutes to whenever really.
It is however dragged down quite a lot with it's peer to peer and ranking system... as some games are literally unplayable due to the lag. For example: One character has the ability to make a forward dash, and become immune to damage for a split second. This can be used to counter other characters abilites, such as nukes, mines or even direct hits if you trigger it right. So in other terms: Something that required timing and skill. With the latency, skill doesn't matter. As you can stand next to a mine, just out of reach. Dash clean through it, end up out of reach, then 1-2 seconds later die, because "you touche a mine, we totes swear.". This lag also can cause no-clips, teleportation or a very common thing: making a blatant miss to hit, whether you dodged it, or are way out of reach. Because you either were in range according to the other player, or you were stuck outside for the others in a "loading" state. I don't know much about programming, but it feels like... having a system that checked "where is character x at 15:42:6 in the game? Back in their base healing? Where did character y's nuke hit at 15:42:6? at the other side of the map? When then it missed." instead of  the current "Hey y, did you hit on your screen? Well then, you died x. Kktnxbye!" So yeah, could definately see some improvements in that sytstem.
Otherwise, it is somewhat balanced game. Mechanic wise, they really ought to fix the recovery issues though. The currency loss on death is just pointless, and only is a punishment on a penalty. Only really promoting hostility towards teammates, and making it literally impossible for certain players to catch up, or get a fair chance. As their enemies will have x2-x4 their health, deal about tripple damage, and have plenty more sustain and support. Sorta encouraging "bullying", as a team can get a huge advantage by picking out a player in the opposite team, and solely focusing all effort on killing them. As then it's basically a 3v2 game, with one team just being way better than the other. Because they have all the currency. It's not helped that "try-hards" or the professional players are in the same bracket. I know this is due to limited amount of players. Especially at certain times. But it utterly ruins the game if you have a casual intent, and run into a maximum cheese, on teamspeak cordinated game, where their team is soelly build to win within 5 mintues, along with making it literally impossible to for your team to do anything about it, as if you even get close to your turret, you die. It doesn't help that cheap, "I win" button tactics exist with certain characer combinations.
That said, the game is only somewhat balanced as said. As you really have a "rock, papper, scissor" system for their characters at times. As some games you can just start, and tell from just looking at what characters both teams have, and conclude that "yeah, we lost/won". As regardless of skill, (unless it's waaay much difference, or unless lag is in your favour) those matches will play out like expected. As there's nothing you can do.
I know most games got imbalance or issues in one way or another. But Awesomenauts could really do with some sort of handicap, or balancing thing. Along with some better way of dealing with the hosting and PtP. As of now, it's really annoying to see a character use an ability towards you, you clearly dodge it, and then you die, becuse it hit you where you were 1-2 seconds ago. Or when you pick up healing, get the +hp, then die, because according to the other person, you haden't healed for them yet, so their damage was fatal on their side, so the game orders your character to die anyway. This is especially not helped by that many people are either gloating, or rude about this. Always claiming it's "skill" when it's positive to them, but suddenly when it's negative for them, it's hax, luck or lag. Becase you know, what's hypocrisy?
Know it's mayhaps been a bit seemingly negative view. But I do really like the game. It just has some glaring issues that could do with being addressed. Also wouldn't hurt to impliment the "Official, unofficial, gg qualifications" as an actual thing. I know some are against it, but overall, it promotes a fun/good game, and demotes cheap tactics. For those that don't know of it: It's basically that everyone gets at least one kill, one death, and one turret down for both sides. While it can be a bit tricky to pull of "authentically". I'd want to suggest making it an archivement to have like, 50-100 games like that, that might could have negative effects... so I can't suggest a good fix to encourage it. But so far, the only good, and really great matches have had these statistics. That, and no gloaters xD Those that had lag in them, at least had the people acknowledge it.
But yeah, overall, good game. But comes with a lot of issues.

After putting some hours in and building up a decent settlement, I have a decent grasp on this game.
Tree of Life is a survival/MMO game where you start on a beach with nothing and then go about punching trees etc to craft various tools. Where the game differs from other traditional survival games is in its scope and depth.
There are a lot of various buildings are technologies to work towards and a slew of different resoruces to gather and craft. The game looks very cute and runs extremely well.
I get a sense of achievement when I make something as simple as a wheelbarrow and find it enjoyable to craft different things that ultimately just help me gather and build faster.
PvE is fun, there are a host of different mobs throughout the world, some more dangerous than others. The combat feels fun and there is a whole host of weapons to unlock and craft, each with their own points system.
PvP is something I haven't done much of. Usually when I come across another player they are friendly but I have had a run in with a few red players that I caught stealing or breaking into other people towns.
The criminal system works well in this game. Basically if you damage something or steal you become a yellow player meaning that towers etc will shoot you and players know you are not such a nice person. Continue this and add in some murder and you are a red player...simple as that.
The game feels very fresh. Its a large open world filled with bases/towns/cities that players have made and try to keep alive. When you build a semi large town the AI will announce raids on you. You can either pay them off with various resources or take on the raid which is fun.
The main thing the games suffers from now is playerbase. I play on the ASIA server and the starting island and a bit inland is quite populated but the higher zones are quiet, but the community is very friendly.
You can basically do anything in this game and they all have seperate skills to level, be it logging, ranching, breeding, farming, mining, blacksmith, swords, daggers, bows, healing, sewing, martial arts and many many many more.
It's a great game, truly my favourite find in 2015 and I look forward to where the developers will take it next.

This game is clearly a labor of love from Larian studios. The story and characters are well-written and, while a little bit derivative in places as most modern fantasy is, has moments of pure brilliance. The cast of NPCs are beautifully written and compelling figures making the world easy and fun to buy into. Even the villains are written well and do not come off as cartoonish or scooby doo -esque, and as the plot twists and turns its way to the ultimate climax you never know who might help or betray you.
This was the first RPG I have really loved since I first played Fable, the Knights of the Old Republic games, or Dragon Age: Origins, and the reasons for this are two simple things.
First, Divinity: Original Sin 2 has a beautiful, complex, and satisfying combat system that rewards your inner strategist while providing the fast-paced, visually stunning effects of action games. And second the game is built around the idea of coop. As a lover of Dungeons and Dragons and other tabletop roleplaying games, this game has earned a special place in my heart for that reason. Coop is simple and well designed, though admittedly it limits the interactions you can have with you chosen NPCs, and really brought the game to life for me. It never felt like the coop had merely been tacked on to the game as an afterthought.
(Additionally, the game has a wonderfully robust modding engine!)
Unfortunately this review cannot be all sunshine and rainbows. D:OS2 is missing several very key RPG factors like customizing the look of your gear with dyes or transmogrifications, as well as missing several key distinctions within weapon groups thaty allow for greater individualization of your character. It also happens to have (at least in my own experience - I had to replay the final boss fight three times to finally gett the ending) bugs that can result in softlocks and being forced to reload saves. This latter issue is one easily overcome by frequent saving.
Overall this is a stellar game and I highly recommend picking it up. I also highly recommend playing with a friend ASAP, it really adds another level to the game.

An excellent RTS game that takes you from the stone age to the modern time. You will go from spears and bows to attack helicopters, battle tanks and nuclear warheads. the idea of only being able to build most buildings inside the territory you control offers a slightly different dynamic to most RTS games, as do the small bonuses you get from accessing specific resources.
The building resources you start out with are the usual food, gold and wood, but as you progress through the ages you gain access to metal and oil, and throughout the game you also need to accumulate knowledge from the scholars at your universities in order to research new technologies.
If the game has one flaw it's that once you become proficient at it you will advance through the ages too quickly to ever really feel like you're in a particular period of history, although you can set the game options to prevent any player from progressing past a specific point. For example, if you would like to wage war with muskets and cannon you set set the game to not progress beyond the Enlightenment Age. If you want to fight the world wars, set it to stop at the Industrial or Modern Age.
Rather than go with a particular historical character, like Age of Empires does, the Rise of Nations campaign allows you to pick any nation and fight for territories to conquer the entire world, from the Stone Age to the Information Age. The Thrones and Patriots expansion also gives you the option of fighting the Cold War (which doesn't really make any sense in an RTS game, to be honest, as this was gets pretty hot), the Napoleonic Wars (as Napoleon), follow in the footsteps of Alexander the Great or the New World.
It's a lot of fun and well worth playing for any fan of RTS games.

How to level up skills:
* means it can be done AFK
-Sneak*: auto-run while crouching into a corner where you fight the goblin shaman in the tutorial, keeping the rats in the pen alive so that they can detect you
-magic skills*: make minimum cost/effect spells of the 6 magic categories, find something to weigh down the cast magic button (for destruction, make the first spell effect heal you for the same ammount the destruction magic damages you)
-alchemy: EAT ALL THE INGRDIENTS!
-Armorer: you can find repair hammers as loot in unowned containers in dungeons and cities, which saves you money...
-Mercantile: ...and then sell merhcants repaired, looted gear you won't use at 2-3 steps up in the haggle slider, selling everything one by one, instead of all at once
-Athletics*: run everywhere until maxed...
-Acrobatics: ...then bunnyhop everywhere until maxed
-Block/Aromor skills: equip shield and armor from armor type(light or heavy) that you will use...
-Blade/Blunt weapons: ...and block enemy attacks until they stagger, then hit them with the lowest damage weapon from the class you'll use(clubs or rusty iron daggers are my recommendation) until they aren't staggered, repeat until maxed
-Marksmanship: use your maxed acrobatics to get to a spot melee enemies can't reach you, use a rusty iron bow and iron arrows, and turn them into pincussions
-Security: get the Skeleton Key from Nocturnal's Daedric quest and this becomes useless
-Speechcraft: spam the wheel choices in the minigame as fast as possible, or ignore this and use Charm spells from Illusion
-Hand-to-Hand: Embrace your inner Rocky Balboa, only carrying a silver weapon until you reach skill level 50, which allows you to harm normal weapon immune creatures.

Like others here already said: Don't let the cute visuals and characters fool you!
This game has the potential to ruin friendships, start wars and to induce eternal despair and suffering!
At its core, it's a simple board game with 4 players. You move around the board by rolling a dice to battle enemies or other players and to land on certain event fields. The goal is to either get an increasing amount of stars or win an increasing amount of battles several times before the others and land on a home base in the end.
Additionally, the wide variety of cards you can play each round spice things up and can turn around a game at any time. For example someone who was in last place the entire time can suddenly be in the lead and finish the game before you can even say "What the...?". Furthermore, there will always be a Poppo to steal your stars when you least expect it! The RNG is strong with this one, so don't forget to pack a whole lot of luck once you start playing and always pray to RNGesus!
But despite all the RNGness and possible rage and frustration you
will encounter sometimes, this game can be really addicting and a lot of fun! Especially with some friends! The really charming characters are a really nice treat aswell! Also... pudding!
Oh and this game also gets a constant flow of bugfixes and content updates which is pretty neat!

DOS2 is fabulous. The game takes a little bit of time for it to click, but when it does you'll be unable to put it down. It's well crafted and doesn't hold your hand on what to do next, sometimes to a fault. However, there are so many ways to approach a situation that there isn't really a wrong way to play the game. Choices matter a great deal and many times I've wanted to go back and explore "what happens if I do this instead?"
DOS2 is also very difficult. I played on the easiest mode possible just to figure out the mechanics of the game. The combat isn't hard to figure out, but difficult to master. There are tons of ways different abilities can synergize with each other than encourages experimentation to a great degree, but also integrate well with how you build your character.
The graphical quality is outstanding, but sometimes can get a little over the top in the second half of the game where your entire screen may be taken up with fire. The lowest my framerate dipped in those situations was about 40 when the rest of the game would run at 60 normally without any issue. The quality of the game's story and voice acting are equally as impressive. A grand epic woven around interesting characters that you can help determine the fates of. I don't think I've played a game with such an engrossing story or characters since The Witcher 3.
If there's something you find awkward or don't like, chances are there's a mod for it. The mod support for DOS2 is great and there are many mods available that help to streamline some aspects that, while probably fine on their own in the game, only help to make the game that much better. A lot of quality-of-life mods can be used to help tailor the game specifically the way you want.
Multiplayer in DOS2 is good, but not quite what I was expecting. At first I thought it was kind of Diablo-like where your character that you work on your own could join with all the loot you had into someone else's game. The actual case is that you join someone's game as a character in their party. I think this design choice is fine, albeit different, but plays well to the theme of the game and overall character based roleplay one finds from D&D-like games. The split-screen functionality is very well done and makes the game actually very playable from a couch co-op perspective.

Simply put, Divinity: Original Sin 2 expands on the best ideas from the first game while taking a complete 180 in tone to deliver a much darker and adult experience compared to the first.
One of the most notable changes is immediately realized as character creation begins, with races, tags, origin stories, and a complete stat revamp giving a new level of depth to character creation. The origin story presets, while not customizable, deliver a unique experience for each. All of the notable "origin story" characters have interactions with each other, and even if you choose not to create them yourself, they can be found and interacted with around the world. Not only this, but you can recruit these important figures of the lore. Origin stories on the surface level seem gimmicky, but allow for a whole new level of replayability, in combination with the tag system. The tag system allows you to acquire new tags that effect quests and dialogue as you progress through the game, or assign them to your custom character in character creation. "Origin story" characters will have these tags preset, as well as a brief synopsis of their lore.
However, the changes aren't just to the character creation. As soon as you get into combat, you'll quickly notice how much has changed. While Divinity: Original Sin 2 keeps the basics of the first game intact, action points have recieved a complete overhaul, streamlining the process of choosing actions. While the new system (6 action points total; 4 action points at the start of encounter. Most skills cost 1-2 action points) may seem to cater to a more casual audience at first, the new skills that accompany this revamp allow for a level of complexity in combat never before seen in the Divinity series. New skills introduced in the second game are more ambitious, creative, and innovative than any in the first game. Even from the start of the game, you'll acquire interesting abilities that you can use to control the battlefield. The new targeting system provided in D:OS2 gives a sense of clarity lacking in the first game. Height advantages and disadvantages means that positioning matters now more than ever before. In addition to the "surfaces" system of the first game (fire, poison, poison clouds, static clouds, electrified water, etc), most of these surfaces can now be blessed and cursed for interesting variations and choice in combat. For example, while fire is harmful to your team, if you bless it, it'll apply a heal every turn and prevent the members within from being frozen.
The campaign here is of absolutely astounding quality and length - my first full playthrough of the game took roughly 80 hours, even without dozens of sidequests. No matter your choice of origin character or custom, you'll find the campaign to be deeply satisfying. However, as noted by the developers, you are meant to play with the origin story characters - and it shows. Each origin character has at least half a dozen unique encounters. While the game is still engaging if you're playing as a custom character, the origin stories really do allow for a better capacity for role playing and it's interaction in the game world.
For the Steam Awards of 2016, this is my pick for the Most Astounding Game. The staggering amount of interactions in the game, even in alpha, can be overwhelming. Divinity: Original Sin 2 could very well shape up to be Game of the Year 2017 for me.

RELEASE UPDATE:
Wow. This game turned out to be the BEST 4X game of 2014.
Really, hands down.
Lots of cool and interesting races and strategies, seriously challenging AI, incredible graphics: this game has it all.
There are still some minor gripes, like the occasional CTD (no biggie, though, since the game autosaves every turn) or the slow performance during the AI turns, but this game is seriously golden.
If you like 4X, you should definitely buy it.
OLD REVIEW:
This game is still in Early Access, so things may change, drastically too.
As of now, this game is definitely incomplete. There's a lot of placeholders, missing stuff, clunky UI and less than stellar combat.
However, this game has a big, big potential.
I really love the graphical style and the lore, a weird mix of sci-fi and fantasy.
City building is fun and the territory mechanic avoids the too often used city spam technique.
Unit variety is good, aesthetically, but not mechanic-wise: everything's the same as of now.
Multi isn't there too, so watch out.
All in all, I'm glad I bought this game: it has potential, it's cheaper and I know I will like it. I can't say I like it now, though.
TL; DR: If you want a discount on the game and you like seeing stuff being built, buy it now. Otherwise, wait: this isn't the usual "early access, but definitely playable", this is a real Alpha.

This is one of the most elegant Civilization style games I've ever played, hands down. It's exceptionally well-balanced, and the difficulty levels truly reflect how difficult it is going to be (ie: hard is pretty hard, even for a veteran player). The game avoids a lot of the "micro-management" aspects that these games tend to turn into, particularly as you get into the late game. There are nice ways to automate many tasks, such as turning on automatic troop production at a building, telling troops at a certain building to move to a certain place when ready, telling bombers or bombardment units to focus on a spot, and good controls for selecting a specified regiment or army with a single click.
Everything from game speed to AI is just very well tuned. There is a wide assortment of different nations, which all have unique bonuses and a healthy number of conquer the world maps and scenario maps to play. This gives the game a huge amount of replay value, so I guess the developer Big Huge Games is an appropriate name.
I can't recommend this game enough if you enjoy the real-time strategy genre.

I have already been playing this game for quite long. The only thing I have understood so far is that the balance in the game is so unfair that the 100% OJ should be given as an example for the term “unjust” in the dictionary! Achievements are another headache. I wish you good luck if you ever try to collect them all.
Still, even though I sometimes really want to uninstall this game and forget about it for the eternity, for some reason I cannot do it. It is challenging, sometimes entertaining enough to make me stay awake for 2-3 more hours after midnight, the characters are cute and have quite different abilities (and this definitely enhances the gameplay). There are lots of various maps to play on, dozens of skill cards to use (and CPUs will use the worst ones on you for sure). However, your luck is just so random here! You will lose one step away from victory all the time, your stars will be stolen by devious Poppo, Tomomo will KO you every single battle, and it is just impossible to describe how evil the bosses are – they can kill you with just one hit no matter what your stats are.
The gameplay is a bit difficult to describe due to insane randomness of all events. You are just trying to survive, collect enough stars or kill enough enemies and then run to your home base without dying every single turn. Being able to play with friends is the best part for sure because then you can at least predict some of their movements. All in all, there are a lot of things to experience in this game. Is it worth it? If you have steel nerves, then yes, absolutely! If you are as weak and competitive as I am, then no, avoid this game like a fire! It will take your soul away.
To sum up, this is a good game that has its issues. And it is dangerous for unstable people. At the same time, it is really nice to KO your friends from time to time. I recommend to buy this game as a 4-pack and play together with your besties (who are, hopefully, stress-resistant).
I also nominate this game as “5 more minutes, please”, while sometimes it can become really addicting. My hunt for the most difficult achievements has already taken about 30 hours, but this way I have experienced lots of different aspects of the gameplay. 100% OJ developers are really cruel people to create such challenges, but at least it makes people really dive into the game and try out all possible cards and moves.

Do you have friends? Do you like a nice board game? Do you like pain loops? WELCOME to 100% Orange Juice.
You play a roll your dice move your mice board game, but when you run into other players theres a short battle, sometimes you can play a modifier card before the battle to modify the chances of winning. You can also play a card before your roll at the start of your turn. Some cards can move everyone around, cause you to roll a specific value, place a trap on the board, or place a piggy bank with a bunch of stars.
Now to win the game you need to do one of two things. You need to get a lot of stars (the points or currency of the game) and keep landing on one of the home tiles, or you need to win battles against the CPU enemies, Boss CPU enemies, or your opposing players.
Now the game can be played single player with 3 CPU players or 4 player multiplayer with up to 3 of your friends (over the internet, sadly no type of couch co-op). There's also a single player story mode where you can play various boards with a loose story for why you are on specific boards, why you are playing against specific players, why the board effects are what they are... It's a wacky time, usually resulting in the persuit of pudding.
But be warned, if you don't take care this may be harder than you think, even on the NORMAL difficulty you will encounted painloops with the story, moreso if you do not go to the in game market and buy (with in game money) booster packs so you can get more cards to modify your deck. There are DLC you can buy, and I highly suggest doing so (especially if the game is on sale like it is as I write this review) as some of the DLC characters are fun to play as and the additional cards from the DLC booster packs (still gotta buy them in game with in game currency, which you only get by playing) add some extra fun when making your deck.

Literally the best game ever conceived. People complain about the DLC policy, but I don't care. I didn't buy it all at once but rather in increments during sales. I've enjoyed every minute of what is one of the deepest grand strategy games I have ever played. After all the enjoyment I've had and continue to have, I feel I owe it to Paradox to set a few things straight in regards to their DLC. Look at the release date. 5 years ago. 5 years of payroll for staff to continue updating a game released 5 years ago. Every dlc has come with free updates. The company needs revenue to provide that kind of support. I see nothing ethically or morally wrong here.
Now, that said, the game. It's a dynasty simulator that will see you trying to grasp onto whatever bit of land you can while maintaining a continuous bloodline of insane, dwarf, Satanist, inbred, possessed psychopaths. At it's heart, CKII is a story generator. Every game is different, every character is different. You could start the game as a lowly count with the genius trait whose progeny will, one day, through their skill in intrigue, diplomacy, stewardship, learning, and martial prowess, reunite the ancient Roman Empire. Maybe you'll found the Kingdom of England, or the Holy Roman Empire. Maybe you worship the Old Gods, in which case maybe you're a Dane looking to loot and subvert Saxons or perhaps those limey brits. Or maybe you long for the days of yore when the Middle East was the center of higher learning in the known world, but tread carefully, the Pope can be kind of a jerk to Muslims. The point is, whatever you choose to play, it will never be the same. Your firstborn son and heir to your throne falls victim to the plague or perhaps assassins. Your brother may plot against you. Or maybe that kingdom you just conquered after a decade of war has 'Elective Succession' and your dynasty loses their claim on it one month after enforcing your demands when your old, ailing king dies.
This game is like an onion. Or a Coen brothers movie. The layers just keep revealing themselves. It keeps being fun.

One of the coolest strategy games of all time. Small pain to get  working on a system with more than 2 GB of memory (easy to fix, just a process), but the game is totally worth it. Units markedly improve as they gain experience, the primary form of currency is POW's (capture prisoners on the field, make money), and I like the emphasis on infantry/ground vehicle/tank combat. It does have aircraft but they're not a unit you directly control. If you're a fan of RTS games, check this out!

Quite simply one of the most exciting strategy games I ever played so far.
With a truly frightening possible scenario and excellent acting in the full motion video cutscenes, you'll think you're watching a movie.
The game takes place in the near future where a worldwide energy crisis has pushed the price of gasoline to the high price of 7 dollars per gallon and the worldwide economy is in a tailspin that terrorists are quick to take advantage of and cause heavy losses.
You play as Brigadier General Jason Richter, leader of the newly formed direct action operations group known as Task Force TALON that is charged with stopping the terrorists and also finding out who's backing them and stop them as well.
The game plays out very much like the Command & Conquer games and other similar titles with the fact that you build a base and then train units that you send out to exterminate the opposing forces, the units will also gain experience and become veterans that can take more damage while also at the same time dish out more.
But one thing to note is that sometimes your infantry units, as well as those of the enemy, can become seriously injuried in the middle of battle and be incapacitated that can lead to them being captured unless they're healed by either a medic or taken to a hospital that you can construct.
By capturing enemy infantry units and having a hospital in your base, you can gain another source of income, there's also banks and treasury buildings that can be garrisoned by both sides that will generate a set number of income until it is empty and when you're in the oil rich areas, you can get money from collecting the oil and bringing it to an oil refinery for cash.
There are some sci-fi units here as well, like the Shield unit which is a form of exo-skeleton that comes equipped with a gatling gun for dealing with infantry units and a rocket pod for the vehicles and many others.
Does NOT run on x64 properly, has issues with more than 2Gb RAM. Is a good game though if you're still running an old OS on a low-end PC.

The gameplay is similar to Civ 5.  Technology progression is a lot more basic, in that there are no dependencies. The only restriction is that you need to research 10 (I think) technologies before progressing to the next tier.  The combat system is really cool.  You can build armies consisting off multiple different units, and then actually control those units in battles. A section of the map is marked off, and all of the units are spread out.  But, if you don't want to take the time to control the battle yourself, you can skip this feature and have your army or unit battle it out like in Civ.  The graphics are great. They did a great job designing the world/tiles.  The terrain can play a big part in battles, which is cool and add a little to the strategy of how you engage enemies. The game is still a work in progress, but I think it's great and I'm looking forward to when it's completed.
